gnmt-human.label: Pakhomova et al. (2004)
gnmt-human.title: Glycine N-methyltransferases: a comparison of the crystal structures and kinetic properties of recombinant human, mouse and rat enzymes.
gnmt-human.proposition: Recombinant human GNMT has measurable catalytic kinetics for SAM-dependent glycine methylation.
gnmt-human.population: Recombinant human, mouse and rat enzymes.
gnmt-human.exposure: Purified enzymes and crystallography; no dietary intervention.
gnmt-human.limitation: Enzyme activity is not a dietary intake-response or proof of brain methylation benefit.
gnmt-human.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

gnmt-ko.label: Luka et al. (2006)
gnmt-ko.title: A glycine N-methyltransferase knockout mouse model for humans with deficiency of this enzyme.
gnmt-ko.proposition: Loss of hepatic GNMT changed methionine, SAM and SAH in mice, supporting its role in methyl-group handling.
gnmt-ko.population: Gnmt-deficient mice and wild-type comparisons; liver assays.
gnmt-ko.exposure: Gene disruption; not glycine restriction or supplementation.
gnmt-ko.endpoint: Hepatic metabolite concentrations and GNMT activity.
gnmt-ko.limitation: Genetic loss of enzyme is not glycine deficiency; SAM:SAH is not a direct measurement of whole-cycle flux. No human dietary dose or brain benefit follows.
gnmt-ko.retrieval_scope: Primary full text Methods/results and PubMed abstract retrieved; n=4 per comparison in reported liver assays.

inulin-glycan.label: Sonnenburg et al. (2010)
inulin-glycan.title: Specificity of polysaccharide use in intestinal bacteroides species determines diet-induced microbiota alterations.
inulin-glycan.proposition: Inulin utilisation machinery changed microbial competitive responses to dietary inulin in defined communities.
inulin-glycan.population: Bacteroides cultures, genetic complementation and gnotobiotic mice.
inulin-glycan.exposure: Purified inulin as sole polysaccharide, and lower-dose inulin with/without other polysaccharides.
inulin-glycan.endpoint: Growth, utilisation genes and species-specific qPCR competition.
inulin-glycan.limitation: Effects depend on utilisation genes, dose and competing glycans. Inulin in a polysaccharide-rich diet did not give the same competitive advantage. No guaranteed butyrate response or health benefit.
inulin-glycan.retrieval_scope: Primary full text Figure 7, Results and genetic complementation experiments retrieved.

inulin-human.label: Kiewiet et al. (2021)
inulin-human.title: Flexibility of Gut Microbiota in Ageing Individuals during Dietary Fiber Long-Chain Inulin Intake.
inulin-human.proposition: Oral chicory long-chain inulin changed microbiota composition in older adults without improving the tested vaccine immune response.
inulin-human.population: Healthy adults aged 55–80; double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
inulin-human.exposure: Two months of defined chicory long-chain inulin.
inulin-human.endpoint: 16S composition, faecal SCFAs and vaccine immune responses.
inulin-human.limitation: 16S abundance is not measured glycan-processing flux; this formulated ingredient is not an ordinary vegetable intervention. Immune endpoints were unchanged.
inulin-human.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and publisher HPAEC chain-length characterization (DP 10–60) retrieved.

fat-vagus.label: Li et al. (2022)
fat-vagus.title: Gut-brain circuits for fat preference.
fat-vagus.proposition: Intestinal linoleic-acid stimuli engaged vagal and brainstem fat-sensing circuits in mice.
fat-vagus.population: Mouse neuronal imaging, vagotomy and receptor-deletion experiments.
fat-vagus.exposure: Defined lipid stimuli; the main intestinal calcium-imaging stimulus was 10% linoleic acid.
fat-vagus.endpoint: Time-locked vagal calcium responses and brainstem activity; receptor/vagotomy perturbations.
fat-vagus.limitation: This is physiological nutrient sensing, not a beneficial direction or a need to increase linoleic acid. Human food-level circuit responses, vagal tone, ADHD and clinical benefits were not established.
fat-vagus.retrieval_scope: Primary Nature Results, Methods context, Figures 2/6 and Extended Data 4/10 retrieved.

meal-nfkb.label: Ghanim et al. (2009)
meal-nfkb.title: Increase in plasma endotoxin concentrations and the expression of Toll-like receptors and suppressor of cytokine signaling-3 in mononuclear cells after a high-fat, high-carbohydrate meal: implications for insulin resistance.
meal-nfkb.proposition: NF-kB DNA-binding activity rose after the tested high-fat/high-carbohydrate meal but not after the isocaloric fibre/fruit-rich comparison.
meal-nfkb.population: Two parallel groups of ten healthy lean adults.
meal-nfkb.exposure: 910-kcal mixed meals: oatmeal/milk/orange juice/raisins/peanut butter/English muffin versus egg/sausage muffins and hash browns.
meal-nfkb.endpoint: Mononuclear-cell NF-kB DNA binding by electrophoretic mobility shift assay; plasma LPS by LAL and LBP.
meal-nfkb.limitation: Small parallel-group acute comparison; multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed. No isolated fibre, fruit or constituent effect; LAL/LBP are not direct proof of gut leakage, portal origin, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit. CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.
meal-nfkb.retrieval_scope: Primary full text Methods and Results, including assay methods and Table 1, retrieved. Random allocation was not established.

carnitine-loading.label: Wall et al. (2011)
carnitine-loading.title: Chronic oral ingestion of L-carnitine and carbohydrate increases muscle carnitine content and alters muscle fuel metabolism during exercise in humans.
carnitine-loading.proposition: The tested carnitine/carbohydrate protocol increased muscle carnitine and altered exercise-dependent substrate handling.
carnitine-loading.population: Fourteen healthy male volunteers; randomised double-blind comparison.
carnitine-loading.exposure: Two grams L-carnitine-L-tartrate plus 80 g carbohydrate twice daily for 24 weeks versus carbohydrate control.
carnitine-loading.endpoint: Muscle biopsy carnitine, glycogen use, PDC activity and exercise metabolites.
carnitine-loading.limitation: Lipid use is partly inferred from glycogen sparing; CPT transport flux was not directly measured. Large carbohydrate co-exposure and extracted formulation are not meat/dairy effects or a routine dietary recommendation.
carnitine-loading.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

ketone-pet.label: Courchesne-Loyer et al. (2017)
ketone-pet.title: Inverse relationship between brain glucose and ketone metabolism in adults during short-term moderate dietary ketosis: A dual tracer quantitative positron emission tomography study.
ketone-pet.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
ketone-pet.proposition: Four days of the tested ketogenic formula increased PET-estimated cerebral acetoacetate metabolic rate in healthy adults.
ketone-pet.exposure: Four-day liquid diet with lipid:protein-plus-carbohydrate ratio 4.5:1, containing cream, milk, MCT oil and egg white.
ketone-pet.endpoint: Dual-tracer PET with kinetic estimates of acetoacetate/glucose metabolic rates.
ketone-pet.limitation: Small short-term nonrandomised study; PET metabolic rates are tracer/model estimates, not direct neuronal oxidation measurements. Combined total ketone energy contribution was estimated separately. No ADHD efficacy or endorsement of routine ketogenic dieting.
ketone-pet.retrieval_scope: Primary full text Abstract, diet Methods and PET modelling retrieved.

flex-exercise.label: Meex et al. (2010)
flex-exercise.title: Restoration of muscle mitochondrial function and metabolic flexibility in type 2 diabetes by exercise training is paralleled by increased myocellular fat storage and improved insulin sensitivity.
flex-exercise.proposition: Training improved clamp-associated respiratory-exchange flexibility in men with type 2 diabetes, but not in matched controls.
flex-exercise.population: Eighteen men with type 2 diabetes and twenty matched healthy men; 12-week before/after programme.
flex-exercise.exposure: Combined progressive exercise three times weekly, 45 minutes per session.
flex-exercise.endpoint: Indirect-calorimetry change in RER during clamp; insulin sensitivity and muscle MRS.
flex-exercise.limitation: No inactive randomised comparator; whole-body RER is an index of substrate switching, not a brain-specific assay. The flexibility change was not significant in healthy controls.
flex-exercise.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

biogenesis-training.label: Little et al. (2010)
biogenesis-training.title: A practical model of low-volume high-intensity interval training induces mitochondrial biogenesis in human skeletal muscle: potential mechanisms.
biogenesis-training.proposition: Six interval-training sessions increased skeletal-muscle mitochondrial enzyme/protein markers and TFAM in young men.
biogenesis-training.population: Seven young men, two-week before/after cycling study.
biogenesis-training.exposure: Six sessions of 8–12 one-minute cycling intervals separated by recovery.
biogenesis-training.endpoint: Muscle citrate synthase/COX activity and protein, TFAM, nuclear PGC-1alpha.
biogenesis-training.limitation: No inactive control, small male sample. These are mitochondrial-content and regulatory markers, not direct counting of newly formed brain mitochondria. Total PGC-1alpha was unchanged.
biogenesis-training.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

arginine-clamp.label: Piatti et al. (2001)
arginine-clamp.title: Long-term oral L-arginine administration improves peripheral and hepatic insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetic patients.
arginine-clamp.proposition: Oral arginine improved clamp-measured glucose disposal in the small type-2-diabetes comparison.
arginine-clamp.population: Twelve lean adults with type 2 diabetes; double-blind study with random allocation into two groups.
arginine-clamp.exposure: Usual diet then placebo; intervention group received 3 g arginine three times daily for one month.
arginine-clamp.endpoint: Euglycaemic-hyperinsulinaemic clamp with glucose tracer; endogenous glucose production and cGMP.
arginine-clamp.limitation: Incomplete normalisation; small selected clinical population. cGMP change does not isolate causal NO mediation. The 9 g/day supplement protocol is not equivalent to arginine-containing food.
arginine-clamp.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

hrv-training.label: Sloan et al. (2009)
hrv-training.title: The effect of aerobic training and cardiac autonomic regulation in young adults.
hrv-training.proposition: Aerobic conditioning increased high-frequency RR variability; post-hoc autonomic effects were confined to men and reversed with deconditioning.
hrv-training.population: 149 sedentary healthy young adults randomised to aerobic or strength training.
hrv-training.exposure: Twelve weeks of conditioning and four weeks of deconditioning.
hrv-training.endpoint: Resting heart rate and high-frequency RR-interval variability.
hrv-training.limitation: Sex-dependent findings, respiration/context-sensitive cardiac proxy, not direct whole-body vagal traffic or universal recovery improvement.
hrv-training.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

mgt-structure.label: Slutsky et al. (2010)
mgt-structure.title: Enhancement of learning and memory by elevating brain magnesium.
mgt-structure.proposition: Magnesium-L-threonate increased hippocampal presynaptic puncta density in rats.
mgt-structure.population: Young and aged rats; associated functional neuronal experiments.
mgt-structure.exposure: The defined magnesium-L-threonate formulation; comparison salts did not reproduce all responses.
mgt-structure.endpoint: Synaptophysin/synaptobrevin puncta and functional release-site responses.
mgt-structure.limitation: Puncta are markers, not ultrastructurally verified contact counts. Formulation- and region-specific animal evidence does not establish that ordinary magnesium foods increase human synapses or improve ADHD.
mgt-structure.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract plus original MIT-hosted paper formulation comparisons retrieved.

folate-flux.label: Stam et al. (2005)
folate-flux.title: Folic acid treatment increases homocysteine remethylation and methionine transmethylation in healthy subjects.
folate-flux.proposition: Folic acid treatment increased tracer-estimated whole-body remethylation and transmethylation in healthy adults.
folate-flux.population: Twelve healthy adults; three-week before/after study.
folate-flux.exposure: 5 mg oral folic acid daily; methionine stable-isotope infusion.
folate-flux.endpoint: Model-based whole-body one-carbon fluxes, distinct from plasma homocysteine.
folate-flux.limitation: Pharmacological folic acid exposure and no parallel placebo group. Not an ordinary-food dose, organ-specific/brain flux measurement or clinical benefit.
folate-flux.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

serine-tracer.label: Gregory et al. (2000)
serine-tracer.title: Primed, constant infusion with [2H3]serine allows in vivo kinetic measurement of serine turnover, homocysteine remethylation, and transsulfuration processes in human one-carbon metabolism.
serine-tracer.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
serine-tracer.proposition: Exogenous labelled serine contributed to methionine and cystathionine labelling in a human pilot.
serine-tracer.exposure: Intravenous deuterated serine and leucine tracers.
serine-tracer.endpoint: Isotopic product labelling and compartmental kinetic interpretation.
serine-tracer.limitation: Intravenous single-person tracer study is not an oral serine intervention or proof of an effective food intake. Compartmental pools and routes are inferred from labelling.
serine-tracer.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

glutamine-null.label: Valencia et al. (2002)
glutamine-null.title: Impact of oral L-glutamine on glutathione, glutamine, and glutamate blood levels in volunteers.
glutamine-null.proposition: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.
glutamine-null.population: Healthy volunteers studied before/after supplementation under a standardised diet.
glutamine-null.exposure: 0.3 g/kg/day oral glutamine for ten days.
glutamine-null.endpoint: Plasma amino-acid and whole-blood glutathione concentrations.
glutamine-null.limitation: Whole-blood glutathione fell; concentrations are not synthesis rates. This does not erase glutamine metabolism, but does not support a universal glutamine-to-GSH enhancement claim.
glutamine-null.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

gln-barrier-cell.label: Li et al. (2009)
gln-barrier-cell.title: Glutamine deprivation alters intestinal tight junctions via a PI3-K/Akt mediated pathway in Caco-2 cells.
gln-barrier-cell.proposition: Glutamine deprivation altered Caco-2 resistance, mannitol permeability and claudin-1 through a PI3K/Akt-sensitive process.
gln-barrier-cell.population: Caco-2 monolayers; inhibitor and siRNA perturbations.
gln-barrier-cell.exposure: Exogenous glutamine manipulation plus inhibition of endogenous glutamine synthesis.
gln-barrier-cell.endpoint: Transepithelial resistance, mannitol flux and junction-protein assays.
gln-barrier-cell.limitation: Cell deprivation including endogenous-synthesis blockade is not ordinary human nutritional deficiency; culture exposure is not a food dose.
gln-barrier-cell.retrieval_scope: Primary full text Abstract, Methods and Results retrieved.

gln-barrier-human.label: Zhou et al. (2019)
gln-barrier-human.title: Randomised placebo-controlled trial of dietary glutamine supplements for postinfectious irritable bowel syndrome.
gln-barrier-human.proposition: The tested oral glutamine regimen improved urinary lactulose/mannitol permeability in postinfectious IBS-D with hyperpermeability.
gln-barrier-human.population: Adults with postinfectious IBS-D and elevated permeability; 54 glutamine and 52 placebo completers.
gln-barrier-human.exposure: Randomised double-blind eight-week trial, 5 g glutamine three times daily.
gln-barrier-human.endpoint: Lactulose/mannitol ratio and symptom endpoints, not tight-junction biopsy measurements.
gln-barrier-human.limitation: Selected clinical population and supplemental free glutamine. Neither ordinary-food equivalence nor benefit in healthy people, brain function or ADHD is established.
gln-barrier-human.retrieval_scope: Primary full text eligibility, randomisation, endpoints and Discussion retrieved; whey-protein placebo noted.

trp-fibre.label: Zünd et al. (2025)
trp-fibre.title: Novel cross-feeding human gut microbes metabolizing tryptophan to indole-3-propionate.
trp-fibre.proposition: Specific fibres altered microbial tryptophan metabolites in donor cultures; responses and metabolite pathways differed.
trp-fibre.population: Sixteen healthy-donor faecal cultures and defined-strain experiments.
trp-fibre.exposure: 5 mM tryptophan plus individually tested fibres at 3 g/L; 48-hour culture.
trp-fibre.endpoint: UHPLC-measured indole products, biomass-normalised comparisons and pure-strain cross-feeding.
trp-fibre.limitation: Inulin did not show the same significant biomass-normalised IPA result as several other fibres. Exact beta-glucan linkage/source requires supplementary-material resolution before a food-class admission. No host exposure or brain serotonin effect.
trp-fibre.retrieval_scope: Primary full-text XML, Methods, Figure 1 and Results retrieved.

minced-beef.label: Pennings et al. (2013)
minced-beef.title: Minced beef is more rapidly digested and absorbed than beef steak, resulting in greater postprandial protein retention in older men.
minced-beef.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
minced-beef.proposition: The tested minced beef increased six-hour dietary phenylalanine appearance versus intact steak.
minced-beef.population: Ten older men in a randomised crossover.
minced-beef.exposure: 135 g intrinsically phenylalanine-labelled minced beef versus steak.
minced-beef.endpoint: Dietary phenylalanine appearance; total plasma EAA and muscle synthesis did not differ detectably.
minced-beef.limitation: One texture/food/population comparison, not a universal amino-acid or transmitter benefit.
minced-beef.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract and retained full canonical PM1-F5 source assessment examined.

cortisol-meal-null.label: Wehrens et al. (2017)
cortisol-meal-null.title: Meal Timing Regulates the Human Circadian System.
cortisol-meal-null.proposition: A five-hour meal delay did not significantly shift plasma cortisol rhythms under constant-routine assessment.
cortisol-meal-null.population: Ten healthy young men under controlled light/sleep conditions.
cortisol-meal-null.exposure: Five-hour shift of three meals; light and sleep schedule retained.
cortisol-meal-null.endpoint: Repeated plasma cortisol/melatonin and metabolic/molecular rhythms.
cortisol-meal-null.limitation: Short controlled male sample; meal-delay null is not equivalence, and does not refute combined light/sleep misalignment. Glucose/peripheral-clock changes are different endpoints.
cortisol-meal-null.retrieval_scope: Primary article Figure 1, protocol and Results retrieved.
